name: Jesus Was Just a Good Teacher?

beats.say: The man who wrote Narnia said there's one thing you can't say about Jesus.
That He was just a good teacher?
Good teachers point away from themselves. Jesus points to Himself. John 14, verse 6:
"I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me."

scroll.text: "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me."

beats.say: In Mark 2, He tells a paralyzed man his sins are forgiven. Religious teachers are shocked. Mark 2, verse 7:
"Who can forgive sins but God alone?"

scroll.text: "…Who can forgive sins but God alone?"

beats.say: Then He heals the man to prove it.
Lewis said a mere man who talked like that wouldn't be a great teacher. He'd be a madman, or worse. Or He is who He says.
Jesus asks you what He asked His friends. Matthew 16, verses 15 and 16:
"But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."

post.yt_title: Jesus Was Just a Good Teacher? C.S. Lewis Said No 📖 #shorts
post.yt_desc:
C.S. Lewis, the author of Narnia, said there's one thing you can't say about Jesus: that He was just a good teacher. Good teachers point away from themselves. Jesus points to Himself: "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me" (John 14:6 NKJV).

When He tells a paralyzed man his sins are forgiven, the religious teachers ask: "Who can forgive sins but God alone?" (Mark 2:7 NKJV). Lewis argued (Mere Christianity) that a mere man who said such things wouldn't be a great moral teacher; he'd be a madman, or worse, or He is who He says.

So Jesus asks you what He asked His disciples: "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered: "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" (Matthew 16:15–16 NKJV).

📖 Read it yourself: John 14:6 · Mark 2:1–12 · Matthew 16:13–16 (NKJV)

post.notes:
- C.S. Lewis (author of The Chronicles of Narnia), Mere Christianity (1952), Book 2, ch. 3: he writes to prevent people saying they accept Jesus 'as a great moral teacher' but not His claim to be God; a mere man who said what Jesus said 'would not be a great moral teacher' but either a lunatic or 'the Devil of Hell', or else He is the Son of God. Paraphrased, never in quote marks ('madman, or worse'). The 'liar, lunatic, Lord' wording is a later popularization and is not used.
- John 14:6 NKJV (bible.com v114): "Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me." Quoted Jesus' words in full.
- Mark 2:5 NKJV: "Son, your sins are forgiven you." Spoken line quotes the short phrase "your sins are forgiven" (partial, in quotes; it is not on a scroll). Setting: Capernaum (Mark 2:1). The objectors are 'some of the scribes' (2:6), i.e. religious teachers.
- Mark 2:7 NKJV: "Why does this Man speak blasphemies like this? Who can forgive sins but God alone?" Quoted the second question; … at the start.
- Matthew 16:15 NKJV: "He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”" Quoted Jesus' words in full. Spoken to His disciples (16:13).
- 'He heals the man to prove it': Mark 2:10-12 ("Arise, take up your bed, and go to your house." Immediately he arose...). Paraphrased, no quote marks.
- Matthew 16:16 NKJV: "Simon Peter answered and said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”" Quoted Peter's words in full; scroll joins 16:15 and 16:16 with … between.
